To submit your story: https://tinyurl.com/bootspub1 Member-only story AI Claude Code UX Product Management Software Development A designer’s full-stack app with Claude Code: live in a weekend, backed up on paper I’ve built a tournament app with Claude Code, but having limited trust in the outcomes, I also asked for a non-digital backup plan. Łukasz Szadkowski 11 min read · Nov 4, 2026 -- Listen Share On a Friday evening I handed Claude Code a brief for a tournament app. By Saturday afternoon the site was up, and by Sunday morning the organisers could sign in with Google. It has a real-time database that keeps working offline, security rules that keep children’s data private, free hosting, and 2,660 tests. I’m a UX designer, and the code was the fast part. My job was the questions a designer has to own: what the app tells a kid waiting for their match, and what happens when it stops working. The app runs a school ping pong tournament in Madrid: kids and parents, three tables, groups and then a knockout, all in about three hours. It has three views: an admin console on my phone, a live view parents open from a QR code, and a big screen by the tables. It also builds its own backup, a spreadsheet and a paper pack. Press enter or click to view image in full size The big screen, the live view parents open from the QR code, and score entry on an admin’s phone. Every name in these screenshots is fictional test data. The brief did most of the prompting I didn’t open with a prompt.
